assessments.reasoning: Section 6.1.4 defines length by counting the String value's 16-bit elements. Textual interpretation gives each element the role of a UTF-16 code unit. The length calculation requires neither decoding into code points nor segmentation into graphemes.

challenge.method: Apply the definition to a surrogate pair and to an isolated leading surrogate.
challenge.results: The pair contributes two elements to length and decodes to one code point. The isolated surrogate is permitted and contributes one element. Well-formed UTF-16 is therefore unnecessary for measuring length.

limitations: An element count is distinct from Unicode code point count and grapheme count. The type permits sequences that are ill-formed UTF-16.
The result concerns the specified String length and does not count display glyphs or user-perceived graphemes.
